payload.name: Resolve deictic time expressions during extraction
payload.description: When a user message states an event happened or an item was received using only a relative time word (yesterday, today, last week, N days ago), during extraction resolve it with the message timestamp and create an event memory.
content: During extraction, if a user message states a concrete event (e.g., receiving/being given something, an occurrence) and gives only a deictic time word such as 'yesterday', 'today', 'this morning', or 'N days ago', compute the absolute date using the message's occurred_at timestamp and create an event candidate (memory kind: event) with that date and the original evidence.

Do not create such a candidate when the statement is just an object mention without an event verb, or when the message already provides an absolute date; in the latter case keep normal extraction with the stated date.
If no occurred_at timestamp is available for the message, do not guess a date; skip the deictic resolution and continue with base extraction.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops facts whose only temporal anchor is a relative expression such as 'yesterday', leaving later 'when did X happen' questions unanswerable. This Skill applies when a user message names an event (e.g., receiving a letter) and gives only a deictic time; it resolves that time from the message timestamp and creates an event memory. It must not apply when the text already contains an absolute date or when no usable message timestamp exists, because the base resolution rule already covers those cases.

payload.name: ResolveDeicticReferencesInEventExtraction
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from a message containing deictic references—relative time phrases ('last Friday', 'yesterday') or first-person plural subjects ('we', 'our')—apply during extraction to resolve absolute dates from occurred_at and preserve all participants.
content: Resolve relative time phrases to absolute dates using the source message's occurred_at timestamp before writing world_start; e.g., 'last Friday' from a Sunday message refers to the Friday two days prior, not the previous day's date.
When the speaker uses 'we' or 'our' for an activity, include all participants (e.g., the speaker and their partner) in the memory content rather than attributing the event only to the speaker.

candidates.solves: Extraction of event memories frequently mishandles deictic references: relative time expressions are assigned incorrect absolute dates, and first-person plural subjects are reduced to the speaker alone, yielding incomplete or wrong memories. This Skill applies during extraction whenever a message like 'we tried ... last Friday' must become an event memory, across any topic. It does not apply when the message states an explicit absolute date or a singular subject, where the base workflow is already sufficient.

payload.name: ExtractEmbeddedPersonalEventsWithResolvedTime
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when a message mixes a general topic with a specific personal event (trip, visit, activity) and contains a relative time reference like 'last year'; create an event memory for the personal event and resolve the time relative to the message timestamp.
content: When a message contains a specific personal experience (e.g., a trip, visit, or significant activity) embedded in general discussion, extract it as its own event memory instead of only capturing the general topic.

Resolve relative time expressions such as 'last year', 'two months ago', or 'yesterday' against the message's occurred_at timestamp to compute an absolute world_start date; record the resolved date in the event memory.

candidates.solves: Extraction drops specific personal events when the message's main theme is a general reflection, so later questions about the event cannot be answered. Applies when a speaker mentions a discrete past experience (trip, visit, activity) with a relative time word inside casual conversation. Does not apply when the message contains no concrete factual event or when no reliable time reference exists.

payload.name: DistinctEventOccurrencesAddNotUpdate
payload.description: When a candidate event is the same type and subject as an existing event memory but is a separate occurrence (different date, ordinal, venue, or result), before choosing UPDATE, verify whether it is a new instance and ADD a new event memory instead of overwriting the old one.
content: When a candidate event is the same type and subject as an existing event memory but is a separate occurrence (different date, ordinal, venue, or result), ADD a new event memory instead of UPDATING the old one; preserve the prior occurrence's time and details.

Before choosing UPDATE/enrichment, check whether the incoming message describes the same specific occurrence already stored (matching time and place). If it is a new instance, create a new memory; only enrich when the same occurrence gains extra detail.

candidates.solves: The failure is that repeated occurrences of a recurring event type are collapsed into one memory, overwriting earlier instances and making later counts impossible. This Skill applies when a session reports another instance of the same recurring event for the same subject (e.g., a new tournament win) with its own date or ordinal; the agent must store it as a distinct event memory. It does not apply when new text only adds detail to the already-stored occurrence (same time and place), where enrichment is correct.

payload.name: Extract explicit life-event dates from narrative
payload.description: When during construction extraction the speaker explicitly states a year/date for a personal or family life event (wedding, birth, graduation, move) inside emotional or reflective narrative, create an event candidate.
content: During extraction, scan user messages for directly stated dates tied to life events (e.g., 'my parents' wedding in 1993', 'she was born in 1987'). Do not skip these because the surrounding sentence is emotional, nostalgic, or photo-related.

Create one candidate with memory type 'event', subject = the person or persons involved, predicate = the event type (e.g., wedding, birth), and the stated date as the event date. Anchor to session timestamp only if no explicit date is given.

Stop after extracting the explicitly stated fact; do not infer dates from vague references, do not extract the same fact from later rephrasings, and do not treat a date attached only to a photo or object as a life-event date.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes skips explicitly stated dates for personal or family life events (weddings, births, graduations, moves) when they appear inside emotional, nostalgic, or reflective narrative, causing the fact to be missing from memory. This skill applies in future sessions where a speaker directly asserts a year or date for such a life event, even if the surrounding text is not factual-sounding. It must not apply when no explicit date is asserted, or when the date refers only to a photo, object, or non-life-event context.

payload.name: RecordPastCompletedEventsFromRelativeTime
payload.description: Use when a user/entity statement describes an activity completed at an explicit past relative time (e.g., 'two weeks ago I read...', 'last month I finished...'). Apply during extraction to record the completed event with a resolved date, not as a current ongoing state.
content: When a message contains an explicit past-time reference (e.g., '<N> ago', 'last ...', 'in <past month/year>') tied to a completed activity verb (read, watched, visited, finished, etc.), extract a memory of kind `event` (or a completed `state`) whose world_start/world_end reflects the resolved past date, computed from the message timestamp; do not label it 'currently' or as ongoing.
Keep a past completed activity in its own memory; do not merge it with memories describing current ongoing activities. If the message also states a current activity, extract that separately.
Stop when the verb indicates a present ongoing action (e.g., 'I am reading', 'currently') or when no explicit past time anchor is present, since the base policy already handles current states.

candidates.solves: The failure mechanism is extracting a past completed activity, anchored by a relative time phrase, as an ongoing state, which loses the completion date. This Skill applies when a future session contains an utterance like 'two weeks ago I read X' or 'last month I finished Y', and the construction agent must record the completed event with its resolved past date so later questions about that period can be answered. It does not apply to present-tense ongoing activities ('I am currently reading X'), which the base policy already stores as current states.

payload.name: Recurring event interval extraction
payload.description: When a message describes a repeated event for the same person (e.g., another doctor appointment, trip, or birthday) and an earlier occurrence already exists in memory, extract the time elapsed between the two occurrences when it is computable from timestamps.
content: During extraction, if the message mentions a second or later occurrence of an event type already stored for the same subject (e.g., appointment, trip, class), compare it against prior occurrences and compute the interval from session timestamps or explicit dates.

If the interval is derivable and the repeated occurrence is contextually significant, add a relationship memory capturing the gap (e.g., 'first and second appointments were N months apart') in addition to the new event memory; otherwise keep the event memory alone.
Do not generate intervals for one-off events, unrelated event pairs, or when the gap cannot be resolved; stop after comparing with the most recent prior occurrence.

candidates.solves: The construction agent stores repeated events in isolation and omits the temporal relationship between them, so later questions about elapsed time between occurrences cannot be answered. Applies when a message introduces a second or later instance of an event type already in memory for the same subject and the interval is computable. Not for one-off events, unrelated pairs, or when no earlier occurrence exists.

payload.name: Resolve-relative-time-dates-in-event-extraction
payload.description: When extracting event memories from messages containing relative time phrases like 'last week', 'yesterday', or 'a month ago', resolve the event world_start relative to the message/session timestamp instead of using the message's own date.
content: During extraction, when a message describes an event with a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'last month', 'a week ago'), resolve the reference date by subtracting the period from the message/session timestamp and use that resolved date as world_start; never use the message date itself.
Prefer a concrete resolved date in the memory content; you may keep a short relative qualifier only if it clarifies recency, but the stored date must be the offset date.

If a later message supplies an explicit date for the same event, update the existing memory to that explicit date (do not add a duplicate); do not apply this rule to absolute dates or to non-temporal uses of 'last' (e.g., 'my last tournament').

candidates.solves: When constructing event memories from messages with deictic time expressions (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'a week ago'), models often set world_start to the message timestamp date instead of the offset date, corrupting the fact. This Skill applies during extraction of event memories whenever a source message contains a relative time phrase and requires computing the resolved date from the message/session timestamp. It must not be used for absolute dates, for sequence-relative phrases like 'my last tournament', or for updates that restate an existing event without a new date.

payload.name: Update ongoing event on completion
payload.description: When a later message describes the completion or end of an activity that was previously stored as an ongoing event without an end time, during extraction and CRUD use the existing memory and update its world_end or duration instead of ADDing a separate completion event.
content: During extraction, when a candidate describes the completion of an activity, search the existing memory pool for an event memory of the same subject and activity with world_end null.

If a matching ongoing event exists, represent the completion as an UPDATE of that memory: set world_end from the message timestamp or stated completion time, and include the duration if inferable; do not ADD a separate completion event.
Only ADD a new event if no matching ongoing event exists or the activity is clearly different.

candidates.solves: Fixes missing durations/end times when a speaker later reports finishing an activity that was stored earlier as an ongoing event. Applies when a future session message states completion of a previously recorded ongoing event with the same subject and activity; the agent should UPDATE the existing event memory with the end date or duration rather than ADD a new completion event. Does not apply when the later message describes a genuinely new or different activity, or when no prior ongoing-event memory exists.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeWeekendDateRanges
payload.description: When extracting an event whose time is stated as 'last weekend', 'this weekend', or 'next weekend' relative to the message timestamp, use this to resolve the correct Saturday-Sunday range before storing the memory.
content: When a candidate event contains a relative weekend phrase ('last weekend', 'this weekend', 'next weekend'), resolve it against the message timestamp as a Saturday-to-Sunday range: 'last weekend' = the Sat-Sun immediately preceding the message date; 'this weekend' = the Sat-Sun containing the message date if it falls on Sat/Sun, otherwise the upcoming Sat-Sun; 'next weekend' = the Sat-Sun after 'this weekend'. Never include Monday in the weekend range.

Store the resolved Saturday and Sunday dates in world_start/world_end and in the memory content. If the intended weekend is ambiguous, preserve the source phrase in the content instead of inventing a shifted date.

candidates.solves: Extraction sometimes miscalculates relative weekend references, shifting events by a day (e.g., treating 'last weekend' as Sunday-Monday instead of Saturday-Sunday). This Skill applies when constructing event memories from messages that use 'last/this/next weekend' and need a Saturday-Sunday range anchored to the message timestamp. It does not apply to absolute dates, named holidays, or multi-day events that are not weekend-relative.

payload.name: Resolve relative dates to absolute event dates
payload.description: Use when extracting event memories and the source message states a relative time (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday', 'three days ago') with a known message/session timestamp; resolve it to the actual date for world_start instead of using the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, when an event's timing comes from a relative expression (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday', 'a couple of days ago') and the message/session timestamp provides the anchor, resolve the expression to its actual calendar date (using the message timestamp, not the current date) and set world_start to that resolved date; do not use the message timestamp as the event date.
Keep the relative wording in the memory content only as a secondary cue; the resolved absolute date belongs in world_start so the event remains retrievable by date.
When later updating an existing memory, do not overwrite world_start with the new message's timestamp unless that new message itself explicitly re-dates the same event.

candidates.solves: The general failure is that relative time phrases are treated as calendar facts or collapsed to the message timestamp, so event memories lose their true date anchoring. The concrete future pattern is construction of an event memory from a message that uses 'last Friday', 'yesterday', or similar relative terms with a known message timestamp. It must not apply when the message gives an explicit date or when the relative expression cannot be resolved to a specific day.

payload.name: Resolve relative dates in memory content
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories, if a plan/event claim uses a relative calendar phrase such as 'next month' or 'tomorrow' that can be anchored to the message/session timestamp, replace it with the absolute date in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if a candidate memory's content contains a relative calendar expression (e.g., 'next month', 'tomorrow', 'last week', 'this Friday') and the source message has a timestamp, resolve the expression to an absolute date (e.g., 'September 2023', '2023-09-01') in the content string, and align world_start/world_end with that date.

Do not keep the relative phrase in the final memory content when the absolute anchor is known; the memory must be answerable on its own. If no reliable anchor exists or the expression is vague (e.g., 'someday'), retain the phrase and do not invent a date.

candidates.solves: A construction agent often extracts a plan or event claim, computes world_start from a relative phrase like 'next month', but leaves the relative phrase in the content, so later questions about the date cannot be answered from memory. This Skill applies when a candidate memory for a future plan/event contains a calendar-relative expression anchored to the message timestamp; it resolves that expression to an absolute date in the content. It does not apply when the expression has no clear temporal anchor or the timestamp is unavailable.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeDurationToAbsoluteYear
payload.description: When a message includes a numeric relative duration (e.g., 'for 3 years') and a message/session timestamp is available, compute and store the implied absolute start year during memory extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message states a concrete duration (e.g., 'for N years/months') and the message/session timestamp is known, compute the implied start date/year by subtracting the duration from the timestamp.
Store both the original duration and the resolved absolute date in the candidate content, e.g., 'has had them for 3 years (since 2020)'. Use the resolved year when the duration is in years.
Do not convert vague time references without a number (e.g., 'a while', 'several years'); record only what is explicitly stated.

candidates.solves: When a user reports a numeric relative duration (e.g., 'for 3 years') in a dated message, memory extraction often stores only the duration and omits the implied absolute start year, so future 'when did X start/begin' questions cannot be answered. This Skill applies during extraction to derive the start year from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory content while preserving the original duration. It must not be used for vague durations without a number or for messages that already contain an explicit start date.

payload.name: Extract past-event memories from assistant turns
payload.description: Use during candidate extraction when an assistant message states a first-person past event (e.g., a trip, visit, or vacation) with an explicit time reference and a place; create an event memory candidate with the time resolved from the message timestamp.
content: When an assistant message describes a first-person past event with an explicit time reference (e.g., 'last summer', 'in 2022'), create an event memory candidate; do not skip it because the speaker is the user.
Resolve relative time expressions ('last summer', 'last year') against the message timestamp to an absolute time (e.g., summer 2022) before storing.
Record the event compactly with the mentioned location and resolved time; do not add unstated details or run extra searches.

candidates.solves: The failure mechanism is that explicit autobiographical event claims in assistant messages, such as a vacation to a place at a resolved past time, are skipped during extraction, so no memory candidate is produced and the fact is lost. This Skill applies when an assistant turn states a first-person past event with a temporal expression and a place. It does not apply to third-party events, hypotheticals, or statements without an explicit time reference.

payload.name: Resolve relative event dates from message timestamp
payload.description: When extracting an event memory and the message contains a relative time expression such as 'yesterday' or 'last week', resolve the actual event date from the message occurred_at timestamp and use it for world_start.
content: When a message describes an event with a relative time reference (e.g., 'yesterday', 'last week', 'two days ago'), compute the absolute event date using the message's occurred_at timestamp and set world_start to that computed date, not the message timestamp.
Record the resolved date in the memory content when it clarifies the event (e.g., 'met Anna on 31 January 2023') so the date is not lost.
Do not apply this rule when the event occurs at the message time (e.g., 'today', 'now') or when no relative time expression is present.

candidates.solves: Construction agents often store the message timestamp as the event date when a user describes a past event with a relative time expression like 'yesterday' or 'last week', losing the true date. This Skill applies to any future session where an event memory is extracted and the message contains a relative time reference that can be resolved against the message's occurred_at timestamp; it computes the absolute event date for world_start. It does not apply when the event occurs at the message time (e.g., 'today') or when no relative expression is present.

payload.name: PreserveDistinctEventDatesOnUpdate
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing event memory with a new event whose resolved date differs from the memory's current world_start, during extraction or CRUD, create a separate event memory or keep the new event's resolved date instead of overwriting the existing date.
content: Resolve relative dates (e.g., 'last weekend') from the message/session timestamp and keep the resolved date in the candidate's world_start.

During UPDATE of an event memory, if the new event's resolved date differs from the existing memory's world_start, do not replace world_start with a conflicting date; create a new separate event memory for the new event with its own resolved date.
Only enrich an existing event memory when the new details refer to the same event and date already captured; otherwise the events have different dates and must not share one world_start.

candidates.solves: Construction UPDATE can corrupt an event memory's date by overwriting world_start with an unrelated value when a new message describes a distinct event with a relative time (e.g., 'last weekend'), causing recall errors. Applies when a candidate event's resolved date differs from the existing memory's world_start; create a separate memory for the new dated event instead of merging dates. Does not apply when new details concern the same event/date already in memory, where normal UPDATE is sufficient.

payload.name: Resolve relative time expressions in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event from a timestamped source message that describes it with a relative time phrase such as 'last week' or 'yesterday', use this Skill to convert the phrase to explicit calendar dates and record them in the candidate.
content: During extraction, when a source message uses a relative time expression (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'this month') and has an occurred_at timestamp, resolve the expression to explicit calendar dates before writing the candidate.

Store the resolved dates in the event content (e.g., mention the month/year) and set world_start and world_end to the first and last day of that resolved period; do not preserve the bare relative phrase as the only time reference.
Stop after resolving that expression; do not add further temporal inference or expand the candidate beyond the stated event.

candidates.solves: Events from messages with relative time phrases like 'last week' often keep the phrase and set world_start from the processing date, losing the month/year. Apply when a timestamped source message describes an event using a relative time expression: resolve it to explicit dates, include them in content, and set world_start/world_end from that range. Do not apply when the message already has absolute dates or the expression is unresolvable.

payload.name: ExtractSecondaryRelativeTimeEvents
payload.description: When a message during construction extraction contains a clause stating the speaker participated in an event with others on a relative past day (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday'), create a separate event memory with the resolved absolute date even if the main topic is different.
content: During extraction, scan clauses for relative past-time event statements (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday') naming an activity and subject. If found and the activity is a concrete personal event, create a separate 'event' memory with subject, resolved date computed from the message timestamp, and participants if mentioned. Do not merge it into unrelated existing memories. Stop after capturing clearly stated events; do not infer events from opinions or general statements.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction can omit a speaker's personal event when it appears as a secondary clause with a relative time (e.g., 'last Friday') in a message otherwise about encouragement or another topic. Future sessions may ask about that event date. This Skill applies when a message states a concrete past activity with a relative weekday/time anchor and identifiable subject; it does not apply to opinions, hypotheticals, or statements without a specific event-time anchor.

payload.name: ResolveRelativeTimeInMemoryContent
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating event/state memories from messages with relative calendar expressions such as yesterday, last week, last month, or N days ago; replace them in memory content with the absolute date derived from the message timestamp.
content: When a source message uses a relative calendar expression (yesterday, last week, last month, last year, N days/weeks/months ago), resolve it against the message/session timestamp to a concrete date (e.g., 'May 2023') and use that absolute date in the memory content; do not leave the relative phrase in the content.
Apply this both when forming an extraction candidate and when updating or merging an existing event or state memory in CRUD.
Set world_start to the computed date for events and states; keep world_end null unless the source specifies a duration or end date.

If the expression cannot be precisely anchored (e.g., 'recently', 'a while ago'), retain the vague wording but still set world_start from the timestamp and avoid stating a more specific date than the source supports.

candidates.solves: General failure: relative time expressions such as 'last month' are written verbatim into memory content while only world_start is resolved, so later recall loses the concrete date. This skill applies when constructing or updating event/state memories from messages that contain calendar-relative expressions and a known message timestamp; it must not apply to vague, unanchored expressions like 'recently' or to non-temporal memory kinds such as profiles and relationships.

payload.name: ExtractSpeakerPastActions
payload.description: When a message contains a speaker's own first-person past action (e.g., 'I made ... last week') alongside another subject or topic, generate a separate event candidate for it and resolve relative time from the message timestamp. Applies during extraction.
content: During extraction, identify each distinct first-person past action by the current speaker (e.g., 'I made ...', 'I went ...', 'I cooked ...') even if the surrounding message mainly discusses another person's experience or a broader topic.

Create a separate event candidate for each such action with subject set to the speaker; state the action and the relative time expression as given, then resolve relative time using the message's occurred_at timestamp (e.g., 'last week' becomes that calendar week).
Do not suppress a speaker's own event because the same message already produced candidates for other subjects; one message can yield multiple independent events.

Stop after one event candidate per distinct speaker action; do not extract when the action is already captured in the same message or when the statement is only an opinion, plan, preference, or vague routine.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often drops a speaker's own past action (e.g., 'I made ... last week') when the same message centers on another person's story or an unrelated topic, so that action never becomes a durable event. Applies to future messages containing a first-person past-action statement alongside other subjects; the Skill forces a separate event candidate with time resolved from the message timestamp. Not for already-captured actions or non-specific opinions, plans, or routine statements.
